%4■Description■%1
> The seventh FT prototype, fitted with the Cloud System, which makes high-altitude flight possible on Claudia, a world with the unusual natural phenomenon called the "Sea of Clouds," where such flight was thought impossible.
> Machines capable of flight, such as the flight-type GTs, existed before this machine, but high-altitude flight, let alone high-speed flight, was out of reach.
> The Impulse 7 is the first machine to have achieved it.
> It was not originally built for combat, but its high aerial mobility and maneuverability let it perform well enough in battle too.
> Flying it takes a fair amount of skill, but it is an exceptionally well-balanced machine and extremely reliable.
> That is evident from the fact that many of its mechanisms were carried over unchanged into the later FT variants.
> General-purpose FTs like this one are also fully protected against the CS (Cloud Stream), so they can operate in outer space as they are.
> Most of the early problems in space were solved by adding propellant for space maneuvering.
{x00}

%4■Description■%1
> The black FT piloted by Omega Fokurosu.
> The name "Impulse 4 Kai" invites misunderstanding, but this machine is not a modified, upgraded version of the mass-production FT "Impulse 4."
> That said, it is thought to inherit the Impulse line's design.
> It was most likely redeveloped from the prototype of the mass-production FT lost in the accident at the research institute, but that too remains speculation.
> Still, if it is based on the "Impulse 4," which was designed for military use, the "Impulse 4 Kai" has likely inherited the same design philosophy specialized for military use.
> Furthermore, estimates based on observed data have confirmed that it far outperforms machines of the same size in every respect, including maneuverability and absolute output.
> This is presumed to be because, unlike the mass-production models flown by ordinary soldiers, it was designed specifically for ace pilots.
{x00}

%4■Description■%1
> The "Gunblaze A" is the most representative of the GTs built for ground combat.
> GTs far surpass conventional tank-type weapons in their ability to handle every kind of terrain, and are especially mobile on rough ground such as wastelands and mountain regions.
> On Claudia, a world with the unusual natural phenomenon called the "Sea of Clouds," high-speed flight at high altitude is impossible, so the strength of ground forces had the greatest influence on the course of the war.
> As a result, the GT, which won its place as the principal ground-combat weapon in the last great war, the Third Claudian War, inevitably became the mainstay in every theater and was produced in great numbers.
> Among them, the Gunblaze series spread rapidly thanks to its high performance, even though it appeared only from the middle of the war onward.
> Its greatest feature is probably that, from the start of development, it included variants from A to Z able to handle every kind of combat situation.
> The A type, or Assault type, is, as the name says, a machine for fighting on the front line, and the most balanced, easily operated and versatile of them.
> Accordingly, tactics built around this A type were used on almost every battlefield, achieving many successes.
> One feature of the A type is its high mobility.
> Most Gunblaze machines get their high mobility from the Ground Rollers in their legs, but the A type also has large caterpillar tracks called the "Giga Crawler" jointed to its hips.
> Using these, it can produce astonishing acceleration when charging, while also keeping ample mobility in swamps and on snow.
{x00}
rows.notes: "Ground Rollers" ([jp], leg rollers) not in glossary; capitalized as a system name.

> The "Gunblaze E" is a Gunblaze variant that serves as a field supply unit.
> Conventional supply units could not keep up with the highly mobile GTs, yet holding back to match the supply units would cut into the GT units' rate of advance.

> In short, the idea was to have GTs resupply GTs; and since the GT's characteristics give it excellent mobility on rough ground, it could operate on almost any battlefield.
> It also carries no unnecessary armor, and in an emergency it can become extremely light by dumping its cargo, so withdrawing from the battlefield was easy as well.

> As the name "Knighthood" suggests, the K type's main weapons are sword-centered, direct-strike arms.
> Basically, GT combat centers on firearms.
> However, firearms consume ammunition and so constantly need resupply; carrying ammunition naturally makes the machine heavier, and also brings the risk of it being set off by a near miss.
> What was wanted was a machine that reconciled the conflicting demands of attack power, combat endurance and mobility: one able to fight for long periods while keeping enough combat power to smash even heavily armored enemies.

> However, it is also true that because melee weapons make differences in pilot skill extreme, it became a machine that only suits certain pilots.

> The "Gunblaze O" is a Gunblaze variant focused on airborne operations.
> The two rotors on its back give it the ability to fly on its own, and thrusters fitted around the body give it maneuverability in the air.
> It saw action mainly in reconnaissance and in operations infiltrating enemy territory from low altitude.
> Its vertical takeoff and landing capability also makes launching from ships easy, allowing GTs to be sent into all kinds of situations and broadening the range of operations.
> It does have drawbacks, however: its continuous flight range is short, it cannot fly at high altitude, and it is not especially fast in flight.

%4■Description■%1
> The "Gunblaze U" is a Gunblaze variant with its armor reinforced to the limit.
> GTs had originally pursued agility and could dodge shells and the like, so thick, heavy armor had no place on them.
> However, as GTs became the stars of the battlefield, anti-GT weapons such as machine cannons with high rates of fire and great power were inevitably fielded in large numbers to counter them, and the tactic of laying down barrages so dense that even a GT could not dodge them came into wide use.
> The U type was developed in anticipation of such situations.
> To keep high mobility despite its heavy armor, its propulsion was strengthened, and to offset the resulting drawback of shorter combat endurance, additional power units were installed inside the armor.
> Even so, the short operating time could not be fully made up for, so a mechanism to purge all the additional armor was also built in.
> This lets it quickly turn into a highly mobile machine by shedding the armor at a suitable moment, extending its operating time and, in turn, improving its survivability.
{x00}

%4■Description■%1
> A high-performance GT deployed in combat in the middle of the Third Claudian War.
> It was designed personally by Hakuto Rondo, the creator of the GT.
> Designed with high-mobility combat in mind, it achieves extremely high mobility through integrated control of its hover, thrusters, leg frame and other systems.
> Furthermore, by applying a jet propulsion system, it also has a degree of aerial maneuverability.
> This aerial maneuverability only amounted to being able to change course at will in midair, such as during a jump or descent, but its effect in actual combat was remarkable.
> However, perhaps because the mechanism combines different propulsion systems, its energy efficiency is poor, and its operating time is short compared to other GTs.
> Moreover, drawing out its full combat power depends heavily on the pilot's skill, and with an inexperienced pilot it apparently could even overheat in the worst case.
> In the end, only a handful of pilots are said to have been able to make full use of its performance, a dramatic leap over earlier GTs.
> Yet for those who can handle it, it is a highly reliable machine, and even now, nearly 20 years after the war ended, in the age of the FT, many pilots still favor it.
{x00}
rows.notes: [jp] rendered "Empty Weight" (Gundam spec convention), used for all [jp] lines. [jp] rendered "aerial maneuverability" since the text defines it as midair course changes. [jp] rendered "creator" to avoid assuming gender.
